children: Medtronic Plc (NYSE:MDT) reorganized its Cardiovascular unit into four divisions, removed Diabetes as a reportable segment and showed commercial momentum—narrowing FY EPS to $5.94–$6.00, raising MiniMed growth targets, investing $80M in Pi‑Cardia, expanding Hugo robotics and noting a put–call sell signal.
: Medtronic (MDT) reorganized its Cardiovascular unit into four divisions (EPT, ICT, CVS, PVH) and removed Diabetes from reportable segments; reported commercial momentum across key device lines.
Narrowed FY EPS Guide; MiniMed Sales Rise
: Medtronic (MDT) narrowed FY EPS guide to $5.94–$6.00 and said MiniMed sales rose 17% to $843M; MiniMed organic revenue growth forecast raised to 10.5%.

: Medtronic (MDT) will invest up to $80M in Pi-Cardia to back ShortCut leaflet tech for valve‑in‑valve TAVR to reduce coronary obstruction risk; Medtronic to be exclusive global distributor next year.
: Medtronic (MDT) says its Hugo robotic surgery system is in 35+ countries, got recent FDA clearance, and expects over 50,000 global procedures by fiscal year-end amid ongoing software upgrades.
: Medtronic (MDT) flagged a fresh put–call ratio sell signal after a ~26% rise since late May; recommendation included buying one Oct 16 $92.50 put option as trade idea.
